findings.title: No tests for new localization fallback feature
findings.body: This PR adds a new server-side localization fallback mechanism (custom FallbackLocaleList, ensure_loaded! chain, integration with the patched I18n translate accelerator), but no specs are included in the diff. Regression risks include: (1) FallbackLocaleList#[] ordering/duplication with current_user.effective_locale vs SiteSetting.default_locale vs :en; (2) Pluralization/Fallbacks module composition when both are mixed into I18n::Backend::Simple; (3) thread-safety of ensure_loaded! running inside a per-request before_filter that touches @loaded_locales and LOAD_MUTEX; (4) cache key stability under fallback (translate_no_cache returning fallback-locale values while the LRU cache is keyed only by config.locale). A feature of this scope touching the I18n initialization order needs explicit coverage before merge.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] crashes if SiteSetting.default_locale is nil
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym and embeds the result in the fallback chain. If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil or an empty string (e.g. a half-applied migration, a misconfigured SiteSetting row, or a unit test that stubs the setting), this raises NoMethodError or returns [:en] without the site locale, silently degrading fallback behavior for every request that goes through the before_filter. The method should defend against nil/blank values (treat them as :en or skip), or the initializer should validate SiteSetting.default_locale at boot.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList is a Hash subclass but only [] is overridden
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList < Hash overrides [] to return an Array, but inherits Hash semantics for everything else (keys, each, merge, []=, store, dig, etc.) while the underlying hash stays empty. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and other code may call e.g. I18n.fallbacks[locale] = [...] or iterate keys; those calls will silently no-op or return empty results, masking configuration mistakes. Additionally, since the override is not synchronized, two threads can compute the fallback list concurrently while reading SiteSetting.default_locale - benign today but a footgun if the override ever grows. Either delegate to a plain object exposing only the contract Fallbacks needs, or override the full Hash surface and freeze the per-locale list.

findings.title: Fallback locales are force-loaded on every request via before_filter
findings.body: ApplicationController#set_locale ends with I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!, which calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for every locale in the user's fallback chain on every request. While @loaded_locales.include? short-circuits after the first request, the very first request after boot (and after each I18n.reload!) must parse all fallback yml files inside the request path, inflating TTFB and competing for LOAD_MUTEX with concurrent requests. The fallback translations only need to be loaded once at boot (or lazily before the first translate for that locale); the before_filter should not be the trigger. Consider moving ensure_loaded! out of the request path or gating it behind a once-per-process flag.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! reads @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: The new ensure_loaded! does @loaded_locales ||= [] and @loaded_locales.include?(locale) without holding LOAD_MUTEX, then delegates to load_locale which does take the mutex. If I18n.reload! is called concurrently with ensure_loaded!, the include? check can race against @loaded_locales = [], causing ensure_loaded! to skip loading translations that reload! just cleared. Functionally load_locale will still reload inside the mutex, but the pattern is racy and the dedicated ensure_loaded! wrapper is the obvious place to add a guard if it ever becomes load-bearing. Worth tightening before this method is used per-request.
